messages:
nina_wang: Hey everyone, first-week setup question. I ran `docker-compose up` for the repo that has both Postgres and Redis, but my app errors out with `ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:6379` and Postgres says `could not bind IPv4 socket: Address already in use`. Not sure if Docker or my laptop is to blame. Any quick checks?

carlos: Welcome @nina_wang! Common cause: you probably have system Redis/Postgres running on host and compose is trying to bind the same host ports. Do `lsof -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN -n -P | grep -E ":(6379|5432)"` to see what's using those ports.

nina_wang: Ran that and saw `redis-server` on 6379 (launched by brew services) and `postgres` on 5432. I didn't realize brew started them. What's the recommended approach so I can keep both local services for other projects?

carlos: Two safe options: 1) Stop the host services for now: `brew services stop redis && brew services stop postgresql` then `docker-compose up`. 2) Or change the compose file to avoid binding host ports so Docker uses its internal network: remove the `ports:` mapping for those services. Your app inside compose will still reach them via service name (e.g., `redis:6379`, `db:5432`).

ada_dev: Another developer-friendly pattern is to change only the compose port mappings to non-conflicting host ports if you need host access: e.g., `- \"63790:6379\"` and `- \"54330:5432\"`. That way you don't touch your brew services. But you might forget which port is which.

nina_wang: Hm, our app reads REDIS_URL from .env as `redis://localhost:6379`. If I remove ports from compose, how does the app connect? I'm running the app outside of Docker (local node process).

carlos: Good catch. If the app runs on host, not inside Docker network, it cannot reach container-only endpoints without ports. So choices: run the app inside the compose network (recommended for parity), or keep ports but remap host ports like ada suggested, or stop host services.

ada_dev: If you want to test running app inside Docker quickly: `docker-compose run --rm web sh -c \"yarn start\"` (adjust command) so web container uses compose network and can reach `redis`/`db` by service name. Otherwise edit your .env locally to point to remapped ports while you iterate.

nina_wang: Okay I opted to stop brew services for now and started compose — Postgres and Redis containers came up. But Postgres still refused to start initially with `bind: address already in use` which surprised me after stopping brew. Logs show it tried to bind to 5432 inside container then failed.

carlos: If container still fails to bind, maybe another container or process is holding that port. `docker ps` to see if another db container exists. Also check if you restarted Docker Desktop recently; sometimes Docker-on-mac retains stale containers or VM processes. `docker-compose down` then `docker-compose up -d` helps.

ada_dev: Also check your compose file for `network_mode: host` which would cause containers to use host networking (rare on mac but possible). If present, remove it.

ops-bot: Tip: On macOS the `host` network_mode is ignored by Docker Desktop, but people sometimes use `network_mode: service:web` or weird overlays. Ensure compose uses default bridge network.

nina_wang: Found an extra leftover `redis_local` container from another project on 6379. Removed it and now both start fine. Thanks! Quick question though: for onboarding, should I change my local .env to point to remapped ports or run the web in Docker? Any team preference?

carlos: For onboarding we recommend running the stack as close to prod as possible. Running the web in Docker ensures consistent env and avoids host port gymnastics. We have a `Makefile` target `make dev` that spins web and deps in compose — check the repo README.

ada_dev: If you prefer host dev (faster edit-reload), we usually keep port remaps documented in `.env.local` (gitignored) with a comment. Example: `REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:63790` and `DATABASE_URL=postgres://redwood:pass@localhost:54330/redwood_dev`. That way you don't change repo files.

dev-env-bot: Recommended doc: https://redwood.example/docs/onboarding/local-services explains host vs container dev patterns and has sample `.env.local` and a `scripts/run-in-docker.sh` snippet.

nina_wang: Great pointers. I moved my local .env to `.env.local` with remapped ports for now so I can keep brew services for other projects. I'll try the Docker-run flow tomorrow. Thanks for the quick help and the welcome! :wave:
